tldr: The abstract mathematical benchmark imposes a novel arm-specific triangular-array local-boundary regime: treatment outcomes lie in \([-1,1]\) and control outcomes lie in \([-\lambda/n,\lambda/n]\), with fixed public \(\lambda>0\). The sharp causal risk has scale \(n^{-2}\); the target is its full constant \(F(\lambda)\), optimized over every outcome-independent assignment law and every original-record estimator. Separate normalization changes the causal coefficients, preventing a scalar reduction to published common-width average-treatment-effect theory. A coupled finite-control prediction experiment supplies the reduction while retaining unrestricted within-unit coupling. Analytic early branches and an explicit rational continuum-primal and all-count-dual bracket at three give traction. The indispensable open content is the evaluated global saddle and every optimal control-count law, with lawful finite-record attainers and all-procedure converses. A prospective randomizr or DeclareDesign allocation benchmark is conditional on a user independently supplying and publicly verifying both arm support caps; it provides no evidence for the cap, validated clinical application or generic practical applicability.
gap: Hull and Sudijono et al. solve common-width causal minimax experiments. The precise inclusion and normalization obstruction leaves the shrinking arm-specific target outside a scalar application of those values. The carried literature evidence does not evaluate its shared-count continuum-coupling saddle.
fill: The field deliverable comprises original-record minimax transfer, the globally evaluated \(F(\lambda)\), every count-law equality set and implementable finite-record certificates. A rational post-\(\lambda_\dagger\) bracket combines full-continuum primal control with an all-count dual bound. Early thresholds, a single bracket and a generic occupation program are supporting results; the global frontier is indispensable.
